bench.intro: A test pattern window that checks the display server from the outside: every Wayland protocol, the 3D renderer, frame presentation and input-to-screen latency. Its last report is shown here.
bench.title: Test Bench

perf.bootOnlyFirst: only the first boot so far: {s} s
perf.bootTestAsk: Measure the boot time over several restarts in a row. The computer restarts by itself 30 s after each login screen appears; logging in stops it. Administrators only.
perf.bootTestLine: test: median {median} s ({min} to {max} s, {n} of {of} boots)
perf.bootTestRunning: Boot time test: {done} of {n} boots measured.
perf.bootTestSet: A boot time test of {n} boots is set: it begins with the next restart.
perf.bootsFooter: From the kernel's start to the first frame on the screen, recorded at every boot. The first boot after an update is kept apart: it builds caches.
perf.compatCount: {works} working, {limits} with limits, {no} not working (Compatibility tab).
perf.conditionsFooter: What affects the numbers, recorded with every result. Results are compared only with the same LordBench version.
perf.deskFooter: How long the compositor takes to build each frame, against the refresh period of the display in use ({budget} ms), and how long a pointer move takes to reach the screen (a simulated mouse, 125 reports a second, moves the window; the mouse's own delay is not included). It passes when the 99th percentile fits that period and few frames come late.
perf.deskKeepStill: A test window moves around the screen by itself, first alone and then with every core busy at the lowest priority. Leave the mouse and keyboard alone until it ends.
perf.disk.ram: Memory (tmpfs or the live session), not a disk
perf.dnote.compFits: Alone, 99 % of the frames were built in {p99} ms or less, within the {budget} ms period.
perf.dnote.compInputOk: Alone, a pointer move reached the screen in {in50} ms (median), {in99} ms for the slowest 1 %.
perf.dnote.compInputSlow: Alone, the slowest 1 % of pointer moves took {in99} ms to reach the screen, more than three frames.
perf.dnote.compMissed: Alone, {pct} % of the frames came late.
perf.dnote.compMissedMany: Alone, {pct} % of the frames came late: the desktop stutters.
perf.dnote.compOver: Alone, the slowest 1 % of the frames took {p99} ms, more than the {budget} ms period.
perf.dnote.deskFits: Under load, 99 % of the frames were built in {p99} ms or less, within the period.
perf.dnote.deskInputOk: Under load, a pointer move reached the screen in {in50} ms (median), {in99} ms for the slowest 1 %.
perf.dnote.deskInputSlow: Under load, the slowest 1 % of pointer moves took {in99} ms to reach the screen, more than three frames: the pointer drags behind.
perf.dnote.deskMissed: Under load, {pct} % of the frames came late.
perf.dnote.deskMissedMany: Under load, {pct} % of the frames came late: the desktop stutters while something else works.
perf.dnote.deskOver: Under load, the slowest 1 % of the frames took {p99} ms, more than the {budget} ms period.
perf.fullNote: The quick test takes less than a minute. The full test also measures the disk with a temporary file of up to 1 GB (deleted at the end), decodes every video codec at 1080p and 4K and keeps every core busy for {min} minutes: about 4 to 6 minutes in all. On an SD card it adds wear.
perf.intro: Measures this computer with LordBench, in an isolated helper, under recorded conditions. Each result is compared with reference machines measured the same way, never folded into one score. Nothing is sent anywhere.
perf.keepStill: Other programs change the numbers: leave the computer alone until it ends. It stops by itself near the temperature limit.
perf.liveYes: live session from the USB stick

perf.m.comp_p99: Time to build a frame, slowest 1 %

perf.m.desk_p99: Time to build a frame, slowest 1 %

perf.verdictsFooter: Three separate answers: how fast against similar machines, what works, and whether it stayed stable under load. Interface layout, paint and text shaping time LordOS's own code too, so they are compared only with references measured with the same LordOS version.

report.intro: This is the exact text that will be saved: the hardware and what LordOS makes of it. It holds no serial numbers, addresses, or user or computer names. Nothing is sent anywhere.
share.exact: Below is the exact file that will be saved. It has no serial numbers, addresses, or user, computer or network names.
share.intro: Others can learn whether LordOS runs on hardware like yours. You share it yourself: LordOS saves the report and a page with the steps to Documents and opens the page in your browser, where you open a public GitHub issue with your own account and attach the file. LordOS sends nothing and keeps no account.
share.live: This is the live session: the report says so, and the catalogue keeps it apart from installed systems.
share.noBench: No LordBench result with this version is included: run one in Performance first if you want your numbers in the catalogue.
share.opened: Saved {json} and {html} in Documents; the page is open in your browser.
share.page.footer: LordOS doesn't send this report and holds no account or token: only you can submit it.
share.page.lead: System Information made this page on your computer. Nothing has been sent: you decide whether to share.
share.page.never1: Serial numbers, UUIDs, MAC or IP addresses.
share.page.never2: Your user name, your computer's name or the names of your networks.
share.page.never3: Your files, your folders or anything you typed.
share.page.neverHead: What is never in the report
share.page.shared1: The hardware: computer model, processor, graphics, memory, disks, network and sound devices, and their drivers.
share.page.shared2: What works on LordOS and what doesn't, as System Information found it.
share.page.shared3: Your last LordBench results with this LordOS version, if you ran it.
share.page.shared4: The LordOS and kernel versions, whether this is the live session, and the kind of drive it started from (internal disk, USB drive, SD card…), never its name.
share.page.step1: Press the button below: GitHub's form opens with the title and summary filled in. You need a GitHub account.
share.page.step2: Drag the file {file} from your Documents folder into the "Report file" box.
share.page.step3: Read it all once more: the issue and the file are public.
share.page.step4: Submit it. An automatic check answers in a comment within a few minutes.
share.page.title: Share your hardware report on GitHub
share.savedOnly: Saved {json} and {html} in Documents. Open {html} with your browser to go on.
share.title: Share this report on GitHub
share.withBench: Your last LordBench results with this version are included.
unavailable: System Information isn't available in this session.
uncheckedFooter: Video decoding and encoding and Vulkan aren't checked in this version.
